title: Irreducible Geometry of Higher-Order Correlator Families
abstract: Programmable quantum simulators are beginning to access correlators of increasing complexity, ranging from four-point out-of-time-ordered correlators to even higher-order many-body correlators. The theoretical framework for interpreting such data, however, remains comparatively underdeveloped. Although a variety of higher-order correlators can be constructed straightforwardly, their physical meaning is often difficult to infer. A further complication is that different correlators are generally not independent: some may be mutually redundant, while others may encode genuinely distinct information. These features make it necessary to analyze correlators not as isolated quantities, but as a structured family. In this work, we develop a geometric framework for the collective analysis of higher-order correlator families. By representing correlators as inner products between operator words, we recast each family as a geometry in operator space. The key idea is to introduce conditioning subspaces that separate this geometry into reducible information, already explained by a chosen resolved sector, and irreducible information, encoded in the residual correlator geometry. Focusing on the latter component, we define irreducible volume profiles that quantify how broadly the unexplained part of a correlator family spreads over independent geometric directions. This perspective leads to several complementary forms of conditioning. Canonical conditioning optimally explains a correlator family. Targeted conditioning fixes the resolved sector to isolate a chosen physical feature. Krylov and cross conditioning extend the framework from a single correlator family to comparisons among correlator geometries. Our framework reveals irreducible structures hidden at the level of individual correlator values and establishes correlator geometry as a higher-level description of quantum many-body dynamics.
summary: This work establishes 'correlator geometry' as a theoretical tool for analyzing families of higher-order correlators in quantum many-body physics. By decomposing the geometry into reducible and irreducible parts, it quantifies genuinely novel information encoded in the system dynamics. This framework offers a systematic way to interpret complex data from programmable quantum simulators.
main_problem: Developing a structured framework for the collective analysis of higher-order correlator families, as these are increasingly accessible from quantum simulators but their physical meaning is difficult to infer due to redundancy and interdependence.
main_result: The authors introduce 'correlator geometry' which allows quantifying irreducible information via volume profiles, revealing hidden structures in many-body dynamics inaccessible from individual measurements.
method: The framework represents correlators as inner products between operator words in an abstract 'operator space,' decomposing the resulting geometry using conditioning subspaces to separate reducible and irreducible components.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to general quantum many-body systems, analyzing families of higher-order out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) relevant for studying dynamics in condensed matter contexts like spin chains or lattice models.
key_observables: Correlator families, irreducible volume profiles ($\pi_q$), Gram matrix determinant ($\det G(\Omega)$), and the residual geometry $Q(W)$.
important_parameters: The conditioning rank ($r$) used to define the resolved sector; system size ($L$); and comparison between different dynamical regimes (e.g., free-fermion vs. chaotic).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that correlator families can be systematically organized into a geometric structure amenable to subspace decomposition via conditioning.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the construction of correlator families as inner products and demonstrate the decomposition of the geometry into reducible (explained) and irreducible (residual) components.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by first defining the geometric representation using the operator Gram matrix, then introducing various conditioning schemes (canonical, targeted, Krylov/cross), and finally applying this framework to diagnose differences between known quantum dynamics regimes.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, systematic geometric language to interpret complex, high-dimensional data generated by modern quantum simulators studying strongly correlated systems, moving beyond simple correlation functions.

Figure 2(b) shows the time evolution of the irreducible vol- ume profile under canonical conditioning at r = 1. At early times, the profile is sharply concentrated near small q. The initially local operators have not yet spread significantly, and exchanging two operators within an operator word changes the word only slightly. Therefore, different orderings of the five operators remain highly redundant. Even a small canoni- cal sector then captures much of the correlator family, leav- ing only a low-dimensional irreducible geometry.
